review.summary: The release-readiness chunk delivers real, fail-closed 0.2.4 guards rather than renamed 0.2.3 ones: three new phase-28 commands (two `--require-directional` package consumers plus `check-access-release --phase 28 --version 0.2.4`) on top of the full phase-27 set, a phase-28 delivery branch in review_phase.py that a readiness review cannot satisfy, and a dependency boundary pinned to the immutable 0.2.3 receipt. Evidence is genuinely executed: 105 commands, all exit 0, one continuous run bound to source 5156a408, with `--resume` barred for phase 28. Docs claim no publication or directional live acceptance. Remaining issues are documentation: README omits the actually published 0.2.3 release though it ships inside the 0.2.4 archive, PHASES.md has no phase-28 acceptance paragraph, and CI.md's resume scope is stale.

findings.description: README never mentions the published 0.2.3 release. Line 29 states "The published maintenance release is [0.1.1]", lines 35/45 cite the 0.2.0 and 0.2.2 receipts, and lines 42-52 cover unpublished 0.2.4 and tell consumers to "retain your existing released pin" without naming it. docs/STABILITY.md:31 and docs/DIRECTIONAL_PROFILES.md:5 both describe 0.2.3 as published, and docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.3.json verifies it unyanked. README.md is a packaged archive member bound by readmeSha256 in docs/checks/phase-28-release-readiness.json:703, so the 0.2.4 crate would ship a front page that misstates the current published release.
findings.required_fix: Reference docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.3.json and name 0.2.3 as the current verified published version in README.md, matching docs/STABILITY.md:31, then re-run scripts/check-management-package.py and scripts/check-access-release.py so the readiness receipt rebinds the corrected readmeSha256.

findings.description: A conditional expression is used as a bare statement: `wrapper.verify_receipt(root, path, compiler, require_directional=True) if phase == 28 else wrapper.verify_receipt(root, path, compiler)`. Both branches are side-effecting calls whose return value is discarded, which obscures that this line is the directional enforcement point for phase 28 and invites an accidental edit that drops the flag.
findings.required_fix: Replace with a single call: `wrapper.verify_receipt(root, path, compiler, require_directional=phase == 28)`.

findings.description: The interrupted-qualification section documents `--resume` for "active phases 23-25" only, while tools/check_phase.py:895 also permits phase 27, and phase 28 is deliberately excluded. The deliberate exclusion of phase 28 (so release readiness cannot be assembled from a checkpointed prefix) is a meaningful property that is nowhere documented.
findings.required_fix: Update docs/CI.md:327-337 to state the actual permitted set (23-25 and 27) and record that phase 28 requires a single complete run with no checkpoint reuse.

findings.description: The maintenance section gives explicit acceptance paragraphs for phase 26 (lines 278-281) and phase 27 (lines 283-289) but none for phase 28; it only says phase 28 "gates its release and delivery" and that package consumers are deferred to it. AGENTS.md:3 makes PHASES.md the document to read before implementation or review, yet phase 28's requirements (directional consumers on both compilers, 0.2.4 readiness review, registry/tag/49 CI contexts) appear only in docs/RELEASE.md:188-203, docs/CI.md:339-346 and the plan.
findings.required_fix: Add a phase-28 acceptance paragraph to docs/PHASES.md mirroring the phase 26/27 entries, naming both chunks, the version-specific 0.2.4 guards, and the exact delivery evidence required.

findings.description: The dependency gate audits only the root lockfile (`lock_path = ROOT/'Cargo.lock'`). contracts/native-probes/Cargo.lock was updated in this chunk to the same patched TLS versions (rustls-webpki 0.103.16 at line 1123, webpki-root-certs 1.0.10 at line 1773) but is never independently audited, so a future advisory affecting only the probe lockfile would not fail the phase-28 dependency check even though the native-probes feature is built in the CI matrix.
findings.required_fix: Extend scripts/check-dependencies.py to audit contracts/native-probes/Cargo.lock as a second lockfile input and record its digest in the receipt, or document in docs/CI.md why the probe lockfile is excluded from the advisory gate.

evidence: docs/checks/phase-28.json: 105 recorded commands (210 matches across "invocation"/"exit_code"), zero matches for "exit_code": non-zero, zero for "timeout": true or "source_unchanged": false; header binds phase 28 to source_sha256 5156a408ada0d03ea16fc6fe82f16f0cbfc0f6a4c7d7b6792dd17ad80588f60c with passed true.

Execution is continuous and real, not reused: first check executed_at 2026-10-22T11:34:18, last (check-access-release) 12:53:52 with duration 3.314s; the two package commands took 391s and 373s (docs/checks/phase-28.json:2885,2916). tools/check_phase.py:895-896 rejects --resume for any phase outside (23,24,25,27), so no checkpointed prefix could have been reused for phase 28; no docs/checks/phase-28-partial.json exists.

tools/check_phase.py:319-328 builds commands_for(28) as commands_for(27) with phase-27->phase-28 renaming plus exactly three additions; tools/review_phase.py:222-228 requires [item['command'] for item in checks] == commands_for(phase) and every exit_code == 0, so the recorded set cannot be a subset.

The three new guards are present in the executed evidence: docs/checks/phase-28.json:2862-2891 and 2893-2923 (check-management-package.py --require-directional for 1.89.0 and 1.99.0, each with checkpoint_bindings to its receipt and the retained .crate in .local/package-worktrees/4c85f31e.../) and 2924-2955 (check-access-release.py --phase 28 --version 0.2.4).

--require-directional is a real additional constraint, not a no-op: scripts/check-management-package.py:114 raises unless exactly 5 external consumer indices exist (4 without the flag), and :152-164 requires examples/directional_profiles.rs in the archive, a digest equal to both the archive member and the working-tree file, selectedFeatures == [], a unique in-range checkIndex running in the external consumer root, and a separate `run --example directional_profiles --all-features --locked --offline` inside the extracted archive.

Negative coverage for that guard exists: tools/test_release_024.py:204-232 asserts the receipt verifies, then rejects a wrong sha256, a checkIndex colliding with frozenProbeCheckIndex, selectedFeatures == ['red-team'], and outright omission of the directional consumer entry.

The 0.2.4 readiness receipt is source-bound, not a 0.2.3 copy: scripts/check-access-release.py:30 registers (28,'0.2.4') while rejecting (24,'0.2.4'); :62 reads phase-28-release-package-{compiler}.json; :68 passes require_directional=True only for phase 28; :69-71 requires commit_fingerprint(releaseCommit) == fingerprint(root) and ancestry to HEAD; :82-106 re-derives the archive with the scm-sdk-0.2.4/ prefix and compares every packaged src/examples/README/LICENSE/NOTICE/Cargo.toml.orig byte against both the working tree and `git show releaseCommit:...`; :119-120 requires both compiler proofs to qualify identical files. Output docs/checks/phase-28-release-readiness.json:4-5,704-708 records version 0.2.4, releaseCommit 4c85f31e..., archiveSha256 447ca402..., toolchains [1.89.0, 1.99.0].

The phase-28 delivery guard required by the plan exists and fails closed: tools/review_phase.py:483-489 invokes release_delivery.verify(..., phase=28, version='0.2.4'); tools/release_delivery.py:22 registers (28,'0.2.4') and :190 rejects any other pair; :226-230 calls verify_management_proofs with require_directional=True for phase 28; :203-204 requires a docs/checks/phase-28-remote-ci-run-N.json receipt; :105-115 requires CI contexts to equal the configured matrix exactly with no duplicates.

A readiness review cannot complete the phase: tools/review_phase.py:459-460 forbids --release-readiness with --advance, and :478-479 rejects advancement when review_scope != 'phase'. tools/test_release_024.py:73-101 proves both paths and that release_delivery.verify is not even called for a release_readiness scope, then that it is called with phase=28, version='0.2.4' for a phase scope, with docs/phase-status.json left unmodified.

The exact CI context set is wired and asserted: .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:73 runs `check_phase.py --phase 28 --verification-only --contracts-only`; tools/release_delivery.py:56-69 derives contexts from the inline matrix (24 features x 2 toolchains + contracts-and-package = 49); tools/test_release_delivery.py:109-110 asserts len(contexts) == 49 against the real ci.yml; tools/test_ci.py:546-548 asserts the workflow references phase-28-contracts.json and never phase-28.json; tools/test_release_024.py:70 asserts ci_commands_for(28) excludes check-management-package.py.

The maintenance dependency boundary is implemented exactly as planned: tools/review_phase.py:403-421 pins {26:[23],27:[26],28:[27]}, requires the declared depends_on to match (docs/phase-status.json:8052-8054), and hard-pins the immutable 0.2.3 receipt by version, sourceCommit 14a67541... and archiveSha256 80a58b7b..., recursively verifying each predecessor's accepted review record.

Dependency security is current, not inherited: docs/checks/phase-28-dependencies.json:3-14,47-50 shows the audit ran at 11:36:58 inside the phase run against advisory-db revision 640bf5a9 with freshHead true and vulnerabilities found false; Cargo.lock:1122-1125 and :1771-1774 carry rustls-webpki 0.103.16 and webpki-root-certs 1.0.10, matching CHANGELOG.md:37-40. tools/check_phase.py:361-365 moves the dependency audit ahead of the Rust matrix so new advisories fail early.

Release claims are accurate and bounded: CHANGELOG.md:5-6 and :43-44 state release candidate, not yet published, and that the entry establishes no publication or remote delivery; docs/STABILITY.md:3-5,34; docs/RELEASE.md:188-203; docs/DIRECTIONAL_PROFILES.md:3-7,137-138. Live acceptance is explicitly bounded: docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md:15-23 records 1 verified method (OAuth), four 403 permission prerequisites, no mutations, and "Directional profile create/update remain live-unverified"; contracts/live-evidence.json:4 binds docs/checks/phase-28-live-attempt-01.json, whose report (:27,32-33) shows crateVersion 0.2.4, mutationsEnabled false, cleanupState not_needed.

Governance regressions were executed, not just registered: docs/checks/phase-28.json shows test_review_phase.py 52 tests OK, test_management_phases.py 27 OK, test_red_team_management.py 51 OK, test_management_consumers.py 7 OK, test_management_fixtures.py 4 OK, test_red_team_management_models.py 13 OK, plus verify-contracts.py --self-test rejecting 29 named tampering cases.

Fingerprint scope is sound for this evidence model: tools/review_phase.py:15-16,135-152 hashes tracked and untracked non-ignored files while excluding docs/checks/, docs/reviews/ and docs/phase-status.json, so the untracked phase-28 receipts do not perturb source 5156a408; untracked SDK source would still be caught by scripts/check-management-package.py:63-68 and scripts/check-access-release.py:87-92, which compare the filesystem src/examples inventory against the archive.
limitations: Read-only review: I executed no commands and re-ran no checks. All pass/fail conclusions rest on reading docs/checks/phase-28.json (identical in content to docs/reviews/phase-28-chunk-release-readiness-attempt-01.checks.json) and tracing the registered command set in tools/check_phase.py:319-328 against tools/review_phase.py:201-229. I did not independently recompute the source fingerprint, any receipt SHA-256, or the retained .crate digests.

I did not open the referenced retained archives under .local/package-worktrees/4c85f31e.../.local/artifacts/ or the extracted consumer roots; the directional consumer execution is established by the recorded receipts plus the verification logic in scripts/check-management-package.py:152-164, not by inspecting build output.

Remote delivery is the other phase-28 chunk and is unverified here: no docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.4.json, release-tag-v0.2.4.json or phase-28-remote-ci-run-N.json exists, no docs/phase-status.json delivery/registry_publication block is populated for phase 28 (milestones at :8150-8160 are all pending), and the 49 CI contexts have not been observed on the released source. I judged only that the guards for that evidence are present and fail closed.

Generated model correctness, the additive overlay, the oracle corpus and the schema-graph roots are phase-27 deliverables already accepted at 46/50; I relied on the compiler/test evidence in this phase's recorded Rust checks and on the declaration-level review of docs/DIRECTIONAL_PROFILES.md:28-47 rather than re-auditing crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs or validation/schema_graph.json.

Per instruction I read no credential or tenant-registration material, nothing outside this repository, and no optional .local/typescript checkout; the `verify-contracts.py --baseline .local/typescript` result (extractedBaselineVerified true) is taken from the recorded run.

Phase 24/25 acceptance, the 0.2.3 delivery gate and pre-phase-26 release infrastructure were out of scope and not re-audited beyond the pinned 0.2.3 receipt identity that tools/review_phase.py:409-413 depends on.

I did not evaluate whether the no-op scope_revisions entries (docs/phase-status.json:7890-7987, 8018-8048, 8167+) with from_attempt 1 and content identical to the live scope_evidence are the intended record of replacing phase-26 placeholder scopes; they verify consistently under matches_declared_scope (tools/review_phase.py:268-271) and I raised no finding on them.
